holidays.name: National Vanilla Milkshake Day
holidays.description: Today is for the classic creamy shake that people wrongly call plain. All you need is vanilla ice cream, cold milk and a blender. Add a straw and a sunny afternoon, and you're done. Vanilla is a blank canvas, so you can also top it with whipped cream, cherries or a pile of sprinkles.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial food observance that has been celebrated on June 20 for years. It marks the start of peak milkshake season, just as summer heats up.
holidays.funFact: Vanilla comes from the pods of an orchid, and it is one of the most labor-intensive crops in the world. Each flower has to be hand-pollinated, so the 'plain' flavor is anything but simple to produce.

holidays.name: National Hike with a Geek Day
holidays.description: Scientists, programmers, engineers and other self-proclaimed geeks are invited to close the laptop and head for the trail. The idea is to trade screen glare for fresh air, and to talk about nerdy topics like gadgets, geology and gear along the way. Non-geeks are welcome too, provided they can handle a long conversation about trail-mix chemistry.
holidays.origin: The day was first celebrated on June 20, 2014. It was created to encourage people in tech and science fields to unplug and explore the outdoors together. It has since spread to outdoor groups and workplaces.
holidays.funFact: The day lands right around the summer solstice, the longest stretch of daylight in the Northern Hemisphere, so geeks get the most possible sunlight for their trek.

holidays.name: National Kouign Amann Day
holidays.description: This day honors one of the world's butteriest pastries. The kouign amann is a caramelized, flaky, crackly-topped treat made of laminated dough, butter and sugar. Celebrate by finding a bakery that makes them. Just don't plan to share the last one.
holidays.origin: The pastry comes from Douarnenez in Brittany, France, where it was created in the 1800s. The day is an unofficial observance dedicated to it.
holidays.funFact: Kouign amann is pronounced roughly 'queen ah-mahn.' The name means 'butter cake' in the Breton language, and that is an honest description of the recipe.
